prompt: What does SQL Managed Instance rent you that Azure SQL Database does not?
hint: Look at where the boundary is drawn.

choices.text: A different engine, older and more compatible with SQL Server
choices.why: The engine is the same; the boundary moved.

choices.text: A whole instance, with many databases side by side
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A virtual machine you log into and patch
choices.why: Microsoft still patches it, and there is no login to the machine.

choices.text: A database with a larger maximum size
choices.why: Size is not what separates them.

prompt: Which of these does Managed Instance have and Azure SQL Database lack? Choose all that apply.
hint: Four of the five belong to an instance.

choices.text: SQL Agent and `msdb`
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Linked servers
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Queries naming another database
choices.why: Yes, by a three-part name.

choices.text: `RESTORE` of a `.bak` from Blob Storage
choices.why: Yes, by its URL.

choices.text: Automatic backups with point-in-time restore
choices.why: Both services have them.

prompt: A program connects and runs `SELECT SERVERPROPERTY('EngineEdition')`. It gets 8. Where is it?
hint: Lesson 8 gave 5 for one of them.

choices.text: Azure SQL Database
choices.why: That answers 5.

choices.text: SQL Server in the course's container
choices.why: That answered 3.

choices.text: SQL Managed Instance
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: An elastic pool
choices.why: A pooled database is still Azure SQL Database.

prompt: Why would a company whose application depends on none of the instance features still choose Managed Instance?
hint: Read the network row of the table.

choices.text: Because it costs less than one database
choices.why: Its floor is far higher than a database's.

choices.text: Because its engine is patched less often
choices.why: Microsoft patches both.

choices.text: It answers inside the company's network
choices.why: Right: Azure SQL Database starts public and is pulled in with a private endpoint.

choices.text: Because it offers serverless compute
choices.why: Serverless is Azure SQL Database's; an instance has none.

prompt: The support query ran in `quitanda` and read `delivery.dbo.deliveries`. What is that name called?
hint: Count its parts.

choices.text: A synonym
choices.why: A synonym is a name you create for another name; none was made.

choices.text: A three-part name
choices.why: Right: database, schema, table.

choices.text: A linked server
choices.why: A linked server adds a fourth part, the server.

choices.text: An external table
choices.why: That is the elastic query way, on Azure SQL Database.

prompt: On Azure SQL Database, `quitanda` and `delivery` sit on the same logical server. Does the support query's `JOIN` run?
hint: Lesson 8: what is a logical server?

choices.text: Yes, because both databases share the one logical server
choices.why: The logical server is a name and settings, not an instance.

choices.text: Yes, if both are in the same elastic pool
choices.why: A pool shares compute, not a namespace for queries.

choices.text: No: only the current database is nameable there
choices.why: Right; elastic query or one database are the ways round it.

choices.text: Only with `-d delivery` given on the connection
choices.why: Changing the current database only moves the problem to the other name.

prompt: Orders are placed every 5 minutes from midnight on 1 January. How many orders, and so deliveries, fall on that first day?
hint: The first order is at 00:05.

prompt: One team owns both orders and deliveries, and they are moving to Azure SQL Database. Which answer to the three-part name is the clean one?
hint: One owner, one database.

choices.text: Join the two in the application, with a connection to each
choices.why: It works, moves the join out of the engine and slows it.

choices.text: One database, with two schemas
choices.why: Right: the join stays in the engine.

choices.text: An elastic query from `quitanda` to `delivery`
choices.why: A feature with limits of its own, for when the two must stay apart.

choices.text: A linked server from one database to the other
choices.why: Azure SQL Database has no linked servers.

prompt: Where does SQL Agent keep its jobs, schedules and history?
hint: A database every instance has.

choices.text: In files on the machine's disk
choices.why: They are rows in a system database.

choices.text: In `msdb`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: In each user database, in a table of its own
choices.why: One place for the whole instance.

choices.text: In Azure Resource Manager
choices.why: That is where elastic jobs are declared, not SQL Agent.

prompt: Order the procedures `job.sql` called to make a scheduled job.
hint: Name it, give it work, make a schedule, join them, say who runs it.

prompt: `@active_start_time` is written as HHMMSS without separators. What value starts a schedule at 04:45:00?
Why does the job's step sum only the days not yet in `daily_totals`?
hint: Somebody will start it by hand one day.

choices.text: So that running it twice adds nothing twice
choices.why: Right, and the primary key on `day` would refuse a duplicate anyway.

choices.text: Because SQL Agent passes it yesterday's date as a parameter
choices.why: Nothing is passed; the step decides by itself.

choices.text: Because a step is limited to one day of rows per run
choices.why: There is no such limit; it summed 348 days at once.

choices.text: To keep `msdb`'s job history short
choices.why: History is a row per run, whatever the step does.

prompt: A company has 40 SQL Agent jobs and wants Azure SQL Database. What happens to the jobs?
hint: There is no `msdb` there.

choices.text: They move with the database, in `msdb`
choices.why: There is no `msdb` to move them to.

choices.text: Azure converts each one into an elastic job during the move
choices.why: Nothing converts them; each is rewritten by hand.

choices.text: Rewritten as elastic jobs, or Managed Instance
choices.why: Right; counting them in `msdb.dbo.sysjobs` is the first question.

choices.text: They run unchanged once `MSSQL_AGENT_ENABLED` is set
choices.why: That variable belongs to the container, not to the service.

prompt: A Managed Instance's subnet is delegated to `Microsoft.Sql/___`.
hint: The resource type, in the plural, in camel case.

prompt: On which port does a Managed Instance's public endpoint answer, when it is switched on?
`sku_name = "GP_Gen5_8"` was refused for the instance. What does the provider expect?
hint: Read its list of values.

choices.text: Tier and hardware; the cores go in `vcores`
choices.why: Right: `GP_Gen5` and `vcores = 8`.

choices.text: A DTU size such as `S3`, as in lesson 8
choices.why: An instance has no DTU model.

choices.text: The serverless form of the same name, `GP_S_Gen5_8`
choices.why: An instance has no serverless.

choices.text: The same name in lowercase, `gp_gen5_8`
choices.why: Case was not the problem; the shape was.

prompt: Which `license_type` applies the Azure Hybrid Benefit to an instance?
hint: The provider's list had two.

choices.text: `LicenseIncluded`
choices.why: That is the price with Microsoft's licence in it.

choices.text: `BringYourOwn`
choices.why: The provider refused it.

choices.text: `BasePrice`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `HybridBenefit`
choices.why: Not a value the provider knows.

prompt: At the illustrative 0.25 USD per vCore-hour and 730 hours a month, what does a 16-vCore instance cost in compute a month, in USD?
hint: Twice the 8-vCore instance.

prompt: Match each road to Managed Instance with how it works.
hint: One description on the right is the database service's, not a road.

pairs.right: a `.bak` in Blob Storage, restored by its URL
backups dropped in a container, replayed as they arrive
a distributed availability group, replicating continuously

right_distractors: an elastic job copying each table at night

prompt: A vendor's application is certified against SQL Server only and needs a file on the operating system's disk. Which is the answer?
hint: Even an instance gives no shell.

choices.text: Azure SQL Database, serverless
choices.why: No instance and no disk.

choices.text: SQL Managed Instance in Business Critical
choices.why: An instance still has no operating system you can reach.

choices.text: SQL Server on its own virtual machine
choices.why: Right, at the price of patching it again.

choices.text: An elastic pool with linked servers
choices.why: Pools have no linked servers and no disk.

prompt: Quitanda rewrites its nightly job as an elastic job and moves deliveries into the orders database. What does that make possible?
hint: The two reasons for an instance are gone.

choices.text: Running on Azure SQL Database, with its lower floor
choices.why: Right: nothing left needs an instance.

choices.text: Turning off the backups, since the job keeps totals
choices.why: Totals are not a backup.

choices.text: Using the DTU model on Managed Instance
choices.why: Managed Instance has no DTU model.

choices.text: Removing the need for any index
choices.why: The support query still needs its index.
